clue.text: The guard's job is plainly to observe somebody after dark

definitions.text: The guard's job is plainly to observe somebody after dark

parts.words: The guard's job is plainly to observe somebody after dark
parts.note: read literally, the name of this guard says what he does: he keeps an eye on a person during the dark hours

explanation.surface: A security guard's duties are simply to keep watch on people at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is taken word by word: watching a man at night. 'Plainly' tells you to read the job title literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard posted to keep watch through the dark hours is exactly what the title describes.

clue.text: Ring changes on what is to be paid for although it is not outgoing

indicators.note: the word Ring changes, its letters rearranged into a new order

parts.words: what is to be paid for
parts.note: money owing is money still to be paid

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers change the order of peals, and someone mentions a bill that is not yet settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests bell-ringing changes; 'changes' is the anagram signal and 'on' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something growing inward, like a toenail, is the opposite of growing outward.

clue.text: The point in things to be worn is that they produce antipathetic feelings

indicators.note: the point letter goes in among the letters of the headgear word

parts.note: hats are things worn on the head
E is a point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: A remark that pointy clothing provokes dislike in those who see it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate is to feel strong dislike, so hates are feelings of antipathy.

clue.text: A serviceman with a poem about a receptacle is a climber

parts.note: WO is a warrant officer, a serviceman

indicators.note: the poem's letters go round the container word

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a bin is a receptacle for rubbish

explanation.surface: A soldier writes verse about a container, and turns out to be a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeysuckle is a twining plant that climbs over hedges and walls.

clue.text: Part of body which gives directions during labour

indicators.note: the compass points fall within the word for hard work, as if happening during it

parts.note: toil is hard labour
N and S, north and south, are compass directions

explanation.surface: Something in the body gives instructions while a woman is giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labour' suggests childbirth, but here it means hard work; 'during' puts the directions inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsil is a small mass of tissue at the back of the throat.

clue.text: Scientist who makes a man a catalogue

parts.note: Herb is a man's name, short for Herbert
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A scientist's work is to turn a man into a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of plants and their medicinal uses is a kind of botanical scientist.

clue.text: Cruel Barbara thus named

parts.note: the heroine of an old folk ballad scorns her dying lover and is remembered as cruel Barbara; this is her surname

explanation.surface: An unkind woman called Barbara is identified by her full name.
explanation.walkthrough: The traditional ballad 'Barbara Allen' tells of a hard-hearted girl whose lover dies for want of her pity.
explanation.definitionFit: The cruel Barbara of the well-known folk ballad bears this surname.

clue.text: Somewhere in London there are men used to fighting over a game

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: knights were armoured men trained for combat
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: In a London spot, battle-hardened men lean over a game table.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHTSBRIDGE is a fashionable district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy district of west London, home to Harrods department store.

clue.text: Dealer who puts me right into fighting and singing

indicators.note: the clue's own pronoun and the right abbreviation are put between the two activity words

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
a chant is a kind of singing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader who sets the speaker straight by getting into fights and songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who buys and sells scrap metal and waste.

clue.text: Clothing which is a different thing to possess around Gateshead

indicators.note: the anagram plus possess word is placed around the single letter
the letters of thing are made different, rearranged

parts.note: to own is to possess
read as Gate's head, the first letter of Gate

explanation.surface: A garment is somehow special to own in the Tyneside town of Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' gives NIGHT, the anagram of the clue's 'thing'. Gateshead is a town in north-east England, read here as Gate's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a loose garment worn in bed.

clue.text: What is left over from times of pure licence

indicators.note: the letters are drawn from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something surviving from an era of unrestrained freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from an earlier time, a remnant.

clue.text: Polished interpretation?

definitions.meaning: the sense here is a shine on a polished surface, sheen
the sense here is an explanatory note on a text

explanation.surface: A slick, refined reading of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a shiny lustre and a marginal explanation of a difficult text.

clue.text: An emblematic woman who makes it with a girl and one in feminine attire

indicators.note: the three pieces are placed inside the underwear word

parts.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment
taken as written
Ann is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A symbolic woman is made from a girl and something else, all dressed in women's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia is the helmeted female figure personifying Britain.

clue.text: Mental, activity inappropriate for Henry. Vill?

definitions.meaning: the sense here is using the mind, reasoning
split into two words, a monarch of slender build, which the famously stout Tudor king was not

explanation.surface: A joke that using one's brain didn't suit the Tudor king.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was notoriously fat, so he was no 'thin king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking is the act of using one's mind to reason or reflect.

clue.text: They are female relatives so men wink awkwardly

indicators.note: the words so men wink are arranged awkwardly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Men clumsily wink at women in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinswomen are women related by blood, such as aunts or cousins.

clue.text: Two names for one who suffers

parts.note: Vic is a short form of Victor
Tim is a short form of Timothy

explanation.surface: A sufferer is given a pair of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is a person harmed or injured by something.

clue.text: One going after a saint into a lake for cover

indicators.note: the saint and the numeral are put inside the lake word

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

indicators.note: the numeral comes after the saint's name

parts.note: St Paul is a saint
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone follows a holy man into a lake to take shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet used for covering things.

clue.text: I put in a message for a piece of meat

indicators.note: the pronoun and the placing word go in the message word

parts.note: a note is a short message
to set is to put

explanation.surface: Someone places a note requesting a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut of lamb or similar meat.

clue.text: Starts, for example, among refuse containers

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits among the letters of the bins word

parts.note: bins hold rubbish

explanation.surface: Something starts up, for instance, among the dustbins.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin is to start something off.

clue.text: Look and retire unusually as one who lingers

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: the word retire is arranged unusually, in a new order

explanation.surface: Look, a person who retires in an odd way is someone who hangs about.
explanation.definitionFit: A loiterer stands about idly with no apparent purpose.

clue.text: It is half up to advertising for it to be brought into action

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of promotion

indicators.note: in a down entry, the half word is read upwards

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: It's partly the advertising industry's job to get things going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DEMI to IMED, which is joined to PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A primed gun or charge is made ready for firing.

clue.text: The factory exists to in-elude a man and his labour

indicators.note: the existence word takes the man and his work inside it

parts.note: is means exists
Ron is a man's name
work is labour

explanation.surface: A plant takes on a man along with the work he does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironworks are a factory where iron is smelted or forged.

clue.text: Public little bit about the time we won

indicators.note: the scrap word goes about the victory abbreviation

parts.note: an ort is a scrap of food left over
VE Day, Victory in Europe Day in 1945

explanation.surface: A small public piece about the moment of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: ORT is an old word for a leftover scrap; VE Day marked the Allied victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in public view.

clue.text: Strand a composer around the point

indicators.note: the composer's name goes around the compass point

parts.note: J S Bach was a composer
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A musician is left stranded around a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a shore, so a beach is a strand.

clue.text: Pronounce happy although born with a smaller amount

parts.note: less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Someone is declared happy despite arriving with less than others.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to declare someone blessed, wishing them happiness.

clue.text: Faint illumination shown by a single amber light

indicators.note: the letters are displayed by the run of words that follows, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A lone yellow traffic light gives off a dim glow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long description of a traffic light, but the definition stops at 'illumination'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a faint or brief light.

clue.text: Drink to lighten me when upset

indicators.note: the words lighten me are upset, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Something to drink that cheers you up when you are down.
explanation.walkthrough: Metheglin is a spiced mead, originally Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Metheglin is a spiced or medicated mead, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: A single, penny used in laying emphasis on preparing building materials

indicators.note: the single and the penny are put inside the emphasis word

parts.note: stressing is laying emphasis
one is a single
D is the old abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A lone penny is used to stress how to prepare materials for building.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-dressing is the shaping and finishing of stone for building.
